subject: c-cont
title: C.CONT.------ALT.F.
description: Diagram in PCC-29, closing the section. C-CONT (composite continuance) is crossed with ALT-F (alternative functionalism), the structural pairing the section has been building toward — what does composite continuance require of alternative functionalism, and vice versa? ALT-F → C-CONT (the crossing). C-CONT → SOC-RT-P (social reality particulars). SOC-RT-P → AFL (affinity alignment) and SOC-RT-P → STF (source transfer). STF → (R)PART (the reality of participation). STF has a *dashed* edge to CULT-INFO-F (culture information focus), and CULT-INFO-F has a *dashed* edge to POL-P (political policies). ALT-F → GRAD (gradualism) directly. Structural argument: composite continuance flows into social reality particulars, which produces both affinity alignment and source transfer; source transfer produces real participation as its primary output. The dashed-edge chain — source-transfer → culture-information-focus → political-policies — registers as conditional: meaning source transfer's drift into culture-information-focus and from there into political-policies is *not* automatic, only conditional, marking the structural breakpoint at which a productive source-transfer can be captured by political-policy-grade definitions. Critically, alternative functionalism produces gradualism *directly* — no dashed edge — meaning alternative functionalism, in Braxton's diagrammatic claim, *will* be subject to gradualism by structural design. The diagram closes the post-Cage continuum's argument by acknowledging the inevitability of gradualism as alternative functionalism's shadow, while preserving real participation as the source-transfer chain's productive output.
